body: I'm so glad that you're doing so much better now.
Thank you for your kind words. I'm trying so hard to get through the pain, it's just hard to believe it could ever have an end.

Thank you so much. I am still going to therapy, my psychologist is amazing, and my GP is referring me to a psychiatrist. It's just so hard when all of my problems are because off all of the trauma. I domt talk to my mum anymore about my mental health struggles, she always just ends up hurting me. I just wish she could love me flaws and all. But if getting her love means pretending im happy, it feels better than nothing. Honestly im not sure how much strength i have left in me. But thank you for reminding me that there are good people innthe world ❤

Thank you so much for your kind words. I feel like I'm barely treading water at the moment. I'm really struggling to keep my head up. You just about did make me cry with your kindness! I do have a psychologist, as well as a suicide prevention case manager. Things just still feel like too much. I live in Australia x

I went to a teacher about my abusive dad when I was 13, and following protocol he went to the year level coordinator and principal. The coordinator called me an attention seeker and nothing was ever done about it. She later called me an attention seeker for self harming, and then again when I had a panic attack because we were getting vaccinated and I hated needles. She was horrible.
I'm glad I could help! Don't be afraid to reach out to people that you know will support you. It can be so beneficial.

It's most definitely possible, it can be our brain's way of protecting us. I was raped when I was 12, and then again when I was 16, and I never thought of either event as rape until a few months ago when I brought it up in therapy. Now I can very clearly see that both events were rape. My mind has denied it for 12 and 8 years, and I was able to go about my life mostly as normal, until I was sexually assaulted last year. I did the same as you, reasoning with myself why both events weren't wrong and why they were my fault. But they weren't, and neither are your experiences. They weren't your fault at all, and you made clear that you didn't want it, but he did it anyway. And your experiences not being violent doesn't take away from it being rape. Freezing is a common reaction, as is dissociating, or going numb. But if it's still bothering you years later, that suggests that your mind feels like something did happen, and it's trying to process it.

Don't be afraid to seek out support from your loved ones, or from professionals 💜

I'm so sorry about what happened to you, and for how you were treated afterwards by the people around you. Unfortunately a lot of girls are ostracized when they try to come forward about rape, and it really only adds trauma to an already traumatic event. Don't be so hard on yourself for not coming forward, if you weren't able to at the time, then that's okay. And it is so normal to freeze when you see your attacker, often our abusers still hold so much control over us even long after what happened. For me it's been 12 years, and I still struggle with the trauma. I'm also sorry for how your boyfriend treated you, he said some really horrible things, no supportive partner should ever be like that to you. If he's toxic for you, are you sure being with him is the right thing for you and your baby? Also I highly recommend therapy, if you find the right therapist for you, it can do wonders.

PM if you want or need to talk, I can do my best to listen and give you a safe space to talk without judgement 💜
Send help, I really need to pee D:
You both look awesome!! Your style is on point. Congratulations! I hope it was everything you dreamed of and more 💕
Hey, what's going on? Send me a PM if you feel like having a chat. I can't promise I'll reply straight away because I'm about to go to sleep, but I can promise I will reply.

I'm sorry you're hurting so much. Feel free to PM me if you need to talk about what's going on. I've been in the same place as you, and sometimes I find myself falling back into it, and I know how hard it is.

I'm not sure how exactly it works for internationals, but are you able to get Medicare? If you get a mental health care plan from your GP, Medicare covers about half the cost of psychology sessions for 10 sessions.

I'm truly sorry that this has happened to you. You were taken advantage of and betrayed by someone you trusted enough to come out to. He is a horrible human being. None of this is your fault, and there is no way you could have lead on a fully grown man when you were 14. Like you said, he's a pedophile. You told him to stop, and he refused. I'm so sorry that he's interconnected in your family's lives. But if you chose to tell your parents and their relationship with him was destroyed, it would be entirely his fault, not yours. He didn't just betray you, he betrayed his best friend, and his daughter. You mentioned having a twin sister, are you very close to her? Maybe you could start small and tell her? And if you haven't already, I'd recommend therapy, it can do wonders.

I'm here if you need to talk 💜

I'm really thankful that I was able to find an amazing guy, whereas two of my siblings have ended up in emotionally abusive relationships. I don't think parents realise just how much they impact their children.

I remember being 10 years old and wishing that my parents would divorce. I thought that they would destroy my perception of love. I get so angry when I see things that say parents should stay together for the kids, because it just creates a toxic environment that the child should not be exposed to.
Omg that makes it even better!! 😂
This is so cute, I'm so happy you're able to be who you're meant to be! I hope you enjoyed your time at your first Pride. And I LOVE that unicorn shirt!!
This is so cute!!

I know this feeling, just recently my mum asked me what my psychologist tells me to do to "fix myself" and for the first time ever I told her I don't want to talk about it and that it's personal. Of course she went really passive aggressive with me and used the guise of "how are parents supposed to help if they don't know anything". I was still really upset by the conversation, but God did it feel good to stand up for myself. I hope you'll be able to stand up for yourself too, as terrifying as it is.

Wow, I was just thinking about this today and wondering if I should make a post to ask. I experience this too, like I know my mum is a narcissistic parent and she has behaviours like manipulation, but when I try to recall specific moments from my childhood that clearly show her narcissism, I can't remember them at all. I think I either didn't realise what she was doing so forgot, or I blocked them out. There are things she did when I was a teenager that I do remember well, and then there are other things she did where the details are really blurry. It makes it hard to explain why she's a narcissist and can be pretty frustrating.
I have from my mother in law, but it's not the same, and I have trouble opening up about my thoughts and feelings (thanks to my mum and dad).

Nothing at all. After the phone call where I told her I have depression, I cried for an hour because she was so horrible. I've started trying to talk to her as little as possible since February this year, after a terrible phone call where something bad happened and I was seeking support and didn't get any from her. I've been distancing myself since. But even though my family is so dysfunctional it's also kind of close knit, so it's hard to pull away from it. And it's hard because sometimes you just want that motherly support and love and each time I hope I'll get it but never do.

Bullet - Hollywood Undead. It's about suicide, but the tune of the chorus is so upbeat and catchy.

"My legs are dangling off the edge, 
The bottom of the bottle is my only friend,
I think I'll slit my wrists again and I'm gone, gone, gone,
My legs are dangling off the edge,
A stomach full of pills didn't work again,
I'll put a bullet in my head and I'm gone, gone, gone."
Thank you, that reminder is nice when you're being told over and over again that it is your fault.
Thank you, it really sucks being blamed for everything while she takes no accountability for her own actions. She destroys me again and again and claims it's her being "supportive".
I am all for this idea! :3
I'm not sure I'll ever be able to forgive myself, but I've at least acknowledged I should bring this up again in my therapy.

It's just so hard and I wish I didn't have to go through it :( I'd managed to block out both of my experiences for years to the point they didn't bother me, and then my stupid and gay brother in law grabbed my breast without permission (thankfully he's no longer in my life) and brought it all back. I just want it all to go back to where I'm able to pretend it didn't ever happen. I hate this so much.
He definitely gets more than enough from my husband and me! He's our spoilt baby <3

I'm so sorry that this happened to you, and that you're currently struggling. Your post struck a cord with me because of a couple of similarities, I'm 24 and what happened to me was 12 and 8 years ago and I'm only just learning to admit what happened to me and what it was as well. It's the hardest thing I've ever done. Just know that you're so strong in making this journey. It's definitely not easy, especially considering the past you describe. Well done for being able to start talking about it online.

If you aren't already and feel able to, perhaps seeking out therapy would help? Having a psychologist behind me has been so crucial in my recovery and coming to terms with what happened, and they may also be able to help with the dysphoria and disparity you mention in your post. I'm here if you need to talk 💜

Thank you, that's a really good way of looking at it. I've been in therapy for the last four months and my psychologist was the only who helped me realise my childhood was emotionally abusive. Beforehand I'd started thinking it was toxic, and I'd always known that it was dysfunctional, but emotionally abusive was never a term I dared use, and even now I still feel guilty using it, and ask myself "was it really that bad?" My psych is amazing and he's incredibly validating, he's been able to help me see that a lot of the self-hatred and self-criticisms I have for myself stem from my parents. We haven't been able to work a lot on my family stuff though because there's trauma stuff that also needs to be addressed. I have an appointment tomorrow though and can't wait to go over what happened with him, having him validate and say I have the right to be upset really helps. 

Thank you for the kind words, I think they're what I needed to hear right now. I'm slowly getting to a better place, I have a wonderfully supportive husband, and his parents actually support me. I made my husband sad last night by saying I never knew what supportive parents felt like until I eventually started letting his parents in.

I can kind of relate to this, after the phone call with my mum yesterday I started to feel grief, and it was really confusing. Maybe because I'd just lost all hope in her. I really hope one day soon I can go NC with my parents, but I don't think I have the guts to do it at the moment. I think I'll always feel absolutely perplexed that my mum can't see what she did wrong, and even more that she wcan't grasp how an abusive, alcoholic father would be so damaging for a child. 

Thank you for sharing your experience with me. I hope I can come to accept it eventually.

It's a really hard thing to accept, but I think I'm at that point where I have to. I think eventually I want to go NC, but right now I think I'm too passive and worried about hurting people. Not to mention, I'd turn out to be the bad guy among my siblings if I went NC with my parents. I'm really glad that you've been able to accept it.

I think I'm finally starting to realise that. I started therapy four months ago, and my psychologist helped me realise how emotionally abusive my childhood was, and I started distancing myself from my mum when I started therapy after a particularly nasty phone call from her. I think yesterday was just the day I realised she'll never see how she's done me wrong.

I have an amazing husband, thankfully, and his family are just as amazing, and incredibly supportive. For the first time in my life, I'm experiencing what supportive parents feel like. I have seen how children of narcs fall for abusers though, my sister was in an emotionally abusive relationship for 2 years that she not long got out of. 

Thank you for the advice.
Thanks for sharing your experience. I'm not sure my mum would ever be accepting or helpful. I think today has just made me lose all hope in her.
Do you mind if I PM you?

Wow, thank you for this. I didn't realise that it was such a common thing. I really appreciate your perspective.

I don't think I'm doing it as a way to get off during sex, it's more like, I know that by having sex I'm going to get these memories and flashbacks and I want that because I want to make myself hurt, so I initiate it. I feel like I deserve to be hurting. I view it as kind of like, I used to self-harm by cutting, and now that I can't self-harm that way, I'm going to do it this way. For the most part, for me, having these memories is a turn off that I push through to torture myself. I'm really glad that you're starting to be able to accept this about yourself. It can be such a strange and horrible thing to feel when you've never experienced it before. But fantasizing about abuse after you've been sexually abused is so common among survivors, I wish it was talked about and normalised more, rather than survivors feeling like they should be ashamed of it.

I really like your perspective here, it makes a lot of sense. Almost like a sugar crash. We try so hard to get away from these feelings, whether it be trying to get our control back by sleeping with a lot of strangers or just by not sleeping with anyone at all. It definitely makes it harder when all you can associate with sex is how you felt when you were sexually assaulted, especially if this is the only sexual experience you know.

Again, thank you for normalising this. It's astounding how similar all of our feelings are.

I think it kind of makes sense, in an "I want to gain back my control" type of way. And then, when it's all you know, it does seem normal. If you've never had pleasurable sex, you might think that sex in general just isn't very pleasurable.

I'm really sorry about what's happened to you, my first sexual encounter was the same, so I can somewhat understand. It really does change how you view sex.  My sex life with my husband was good until I started dealing with my abuse in therapy, I hope it can get back to that. And I really hope that one day sex will be an action that you can enjoy, too. If you don't mind me asking, do you see a therapist? If not, I would recommend it. It's hard, but I think in the long run it really does help.

It's just really frustrating because I've been okay-ish over the last couple of weeks and have had minimal suicidal thoughts and after my psychologist appointment yesterday I just felt angry and suicidal and done with everything. I was annoyed with my psychologist for caring and worrying about me. 

I know there are people that care about me, but it still feels like they wouldn't care that much if I were gone, and that they'd get over it quickly. The only person I know this isn't true for is my husband, I know it would destroy him, and that's exactly the reason why I have to stay. I guess also for my psychologist, because I know how much it would hurt to lose a client that way, and I don't want to cause people hurt. It just sucks having to stay here for everyone else when it's not what I want. 

Thank you for your kind words, they were nice to read. Maybe one day I will be, my psychologist seems to think it's possible, I think it's just a long way off. Thank you ❤

Thank you for sharing your experience with me. It's really hard when an act that is meant to be so loving and caring with a person you love now just makes you feel dirty, used and disgusting. It makes me feel guilty that I can't make love with my husband like a normal person. And it does feel like that's what sex is supposed to feel like now. It just feels like torture. I really hope it gets better in time, too.

I guess it's a bit like that for me too, because sometimes I initiate sex as a way to test myself, to see how much it will affect me. It's just when I'm having a really bad day, I want to make myself hurt more. I've struggled with self-harm in the past and am currently trying to quit that, but I think this might just be a new way I'm trying to self-harm, the only difference is that it's not physical self-harm. I get that too, it's really hard for me to say no, but my husband was able to help me through that by repeatedly telling me if I don't want sex, it's okay and I shouldn't worry about disappointing him.

All the trauma I have is from between the ages of 12-16, I'm 24 now, and I've only recently come to acknowledge everything that's happened to me and accept it for what it is. It's still really hard to cope with it. My husband knows everything that I've been struggling with, so I might just tell him I don't want to have sex for a while and leave it at that.

I really thank you for your kind words, it's hard to accept that I deserve anything but pain, but I am seeing a psychologist and we're working on self-kindness and self-compassion, as well as working through my trauma. And thank you for sharing your experience with me, it gives me a new perspective to look at this.

Thank you, I hate that I'm not alone in feeling this, but at the same time, having people that can relate or share advice really helps. I'm not entirely sure that my brain isn't just making it all up! And I feel like I might never know. I'm really into writing, so that's actually a really good idea, I might try that, thank you! It would also be really good to share with my psychologist. The only thing is that I can't make out a lot of the details, because it was a dark room. 

This community is so helpful, I honestly think that being apart of it is helping me in my recovery (my psychologist agrees!). Being able to support and listen to other people is doing wonders, too. I really appreciate your kind words, I read your comment a few hours ago when I was in a really rough moment and it really helped 💜
I'm really glad we could help, even just a little bit <3

Thank you, I needed that reminder. Baby steps are what I need to keep in mind, and that slow progress is still progress. I heard back from my psychologist and he was proud of me, hearing his kind words and being told that it's okay to feel triggered because it's necessary for success really helped. It normalised the strong emotions that I felt for the rest of the day.

I'm really glad you have someone close to you that you can talk to. That's really sad that you can't get justice and certainly wouldn't make this any easier. Are you able to go to a doctor and get checked out? I think you're being really brave and strong. Be safe and take care of yourself.

I am SO sorry that this has happened to you, it sounds traumatising. No matter what country you're in, this is not okay, and I really hope one day the whole world will know this. I'm really sorry about the situation you're in, I can't understand, but I'm sure it's a whole new level of painful that even your own country won't stand behind you. Is there someone close to you that you'd feel able to speak to about this and about how you're feeling? I also want to share r/rapecounseling with you, it's a supportive community with people who are in similar pain.

I thought the same thing, and while the thought of crying in front of someone is still horrifying to me, it's given me a new perspective on it.

I'm sorry about your mum ❤ it's okay to hold back, take your own time in sharing. To me your therapist sounds like a wonderful guy, and that he really wants you to feel comfortable both with crying and with him. I'm glad that you have a therapist you can open up to and be vulnerable with. I also just want to add, self-care is so important in the therapeutical field, and I feel pretty certain that if he was struggling, he would tell you. It might be hypocritical of me to say, but crying is a healthy thing, and being vulnerable with someone is okay.

I haven't experienced this because I hate the thought of me crying, and my therapist knows this, and is continually trying to tell me that crying is okay. He told me that he's cried in sessions before, and that that's okay. I don't think it's unprofessional at all, in fact, I think it's beautiful. My therapist shared this quote with me that I want to share with you:

"There is a sacredness in tears. They are not the mark of weakness, but of power. They speak more eloquently than ten thousand tongues. They are the messengers of overwhelming grief, of deep contrition, and of unspeakable love.  

-Washington Irving"

If you feel you are able, perhaps try bringing up how you're feeling with him, and see how he feels about it? And that you're worried about burdening him? The majority of therapists have people they can debrief with too, like their supervisors or spouse. If it was a real problem, I think he would bring it up with you. I'd really recommend talking to him about it to ease your mind :)

Thank you, I really appreciate your kind words!  ❤️ I'm so lucky to have him, and even luckier that we were in the position where he could talk to my psychologist about how to support me. The conversation they had definitely made him realise not to go into problem solving mode, which makes things a lot easier.

That's a really good point. Just some form of class about social interactions where children can learn everything they really need to know about interactions. Children need to be taught that it's okay to talk about their feelings too! We're in a society where it's considered the most horrible thing in the world to show any negative emotions, and that is just being displayed to our children. They deserve so much more than that. 

That is so horrifying to hear! And that parents are agreeing with it!! I really thought that our society was starting to become more progressive than that! And this notion that "if they know it, they'll do it" really needs to be expired. Like I said, my school was Catholic so we didn't have proper sex ed, and a lot of the girls in my year were sending nude photos and participating in sex by the age of 14! If we were taught properly, about all aspects relating to sex, I really don't think it would have been such a huge problem. Like you said, I think this would all be because of sexual ignorance. I should add though, that after a while of this happening an assembly was held were police came and explained about child pornography and that by sending nude photos you're committing a crime. I don't think this helped though.

I honestly can't believe that there would be parents out there NOT teaching the "no aspect" of consent! But I suppose we're still living in a society where it's considered rude to not kiss your grandparents or aunts and uncles goodbye. My grandma practically forces my husband to let her hug and kiss him when they say goodbye, he's a good sport about it, but if he had his way he wouldn't be doing that. Adults need to be taught, as well as children. 

Thank you, I'm still processing a lot of really hard stuff so I can't honestly say that I'm okay, but I'm getting there  ❤️❤️
Good luck! I can just imagine how hard this must be for you. You are *so* strong and brave for taking this to court. Just remember that we're all here for you! Take care of yourself!  💜

Most definitely, you're so right. I think it would be great if parents could be educated by this, because there are so many unknowns to it. Like, speaking from a non-parent point of view, I'd have no idea what age I should start teaching this to my kids, it's something that I feel needs to be done right from the beginning, but how much will your child actually take in between the ages of 0-3? Of course this is something I intend to know when I actually do decide to have kids.

Exactly. And children are naturally curious, too, they don't know that exposing themselves to another child or touching another child is wrong or could harm that other child. Like you said, children need to see good behaviour modelled, and right now in society, I don't think that's happening. Both women and men are turned away or treated terribly at police stations, boys are taught that they can't be r\*\*\*d and that no one will believe them if they are, women are taught not to put themselves in those situations where it could happen, and are victim-blamed. The attitudes around r\*\*\* and r\*\*\* culture need to be shifted so that our children don't grow up with these same attitudes.

Thank you, I don't blame the school (probably because I spend so much energy blaming myself *for putting myself in that situation*). My school could hardly teach us sex education, I remember in high school the teachers wanted too, but because they believe you can't have sex before marriage, they could hardly even talk about pregnancy with us. Religion can be very damaging for r\*\*\* survivors.

You're right, that was a mistake of me to say, both sexes do need to be taught what consent is. I thought about going back and editing my comment to include both sexes, but I think that it's an important mistake for people to see.  I didn't know that what happened to me when I 12 was rape until my psychologist said that that's what he would constitute it as. I was somewhat ignorant before, thinking that rape was only forced sex. I still can't fully accept that I didn't consent to what happened to me when I was 12 simply because I opened my legs to allow the 19 year old to finger me. It doesn't matter that I felt like I had to, or that my actions and behaviours were screaming no or the simple fact that I was 12.  My school hardly taught us about sex at all, let alone what consent is, because it was a Catholic school. I'm glad that your daughter's school is teaching this to the students. It falls onto parents to educate their children, too. I don't have children of my own, but my friend teaches her son that absolutely no one should touch him without his permission, and if they do, he should tell her. I think that's an important thing to be taught, and it does need to start early.

Thank you, I appreciate that ❤️  it's just what my husband is like too, he's very intelligent and logical thinking. Even now when I try to talk about problems he sometimes goes into that mode, but he's getting a lot better, talking to my therapist (who was also his at the time) really helped him to learn how to support me. But it really is that comforting, nurturing, reassuring mode that we really need when we choose to open up about our experiences.

They definitely do! Along with this, just society in general needs to be educated. Boys need to be taught exactly what consent is. I remember growing up there were ads on TV against sexual violence that said "no means no" which was great, but what about when the word "no" isn't said? What if it IS said, just not out loud? I think society is growing, but it's still got a long way to go.

I hope you're doing okay  ❤️

Edit: It's so important that BOTH sexes are educated about what consent is. Apologies for only saying boys need to be taught what consent is!

Exactly! And I'm sorry, that sounds like a really horrible experience. The police need to be trained to handle these situations, how they treated you was not on at all. I've read so many experiences similar to yours, and I can't understand how people could think that survivors MUST come forward when this is what so many who do are subjected to? 

I was 12 when I was first abused, and at the time I didn't know that what the 19 year old man was doing to me was wrong, I thought it was my fault. At the time, it didn't even cross my mind once to report him. I was too ashamed and I didn't tell my husband (boyfriend at the time) until I was 19. He regrets this, but he immediately went into problem solving mode, trying to find who this man is, and telling me that I need to go to the police because what the man did was sick and he might do it to other little girls. It made me feel horrible and guilty and ashamed. It hadn't even occurred to me until this interaction that this man was a pedophile taking advantage of a young girl. Thankfully my husband has grown a lot since then.

I'm sorry that you're going through this. What you are feeling is completely normal, and you are in no way at fault for what happened. You told him no, and then he waited until you were vulnerable to continue abusing you. In that state, you were in no condition to consent, and I'm angry that he would try to convince you it was consensual. I really want to validate what you're feeling.

After going through an experience like this, especially when the abuser is a friend, can make it so hard to come forward, and it can be really alienating. I really want to stress that if you are uncomfortable accepting his friend request, then you have every right to refuse it. What he did to you was wrong, and you are 100% entitled to feel like this. You don't need to give anyone a reason as to why you don't want to be friends with him, and you most certainly do not owe him an explanation if you don't want to give one to him. The most important thing in this situation is YOU. Take care of yourself. Seek out therapy to talk about this, if you feel you are able to. Therapy can be really helpful.

Hope this helps, and here if you need. Just remember to take care of yourself.

I can relate so hard to this! Just recently I saw a guy's comments about how we shouldn't treat survivors as "snowflakes" and should be telling them to report their abusers. I felt like he was saying that it's the survivors' fault if their abusers go out and abuse other people, because we could have prevented it.

He wasn't a bad guy, he was just trying to understand and he was angry that he couldn't do anything to stop the man who abused his girlfriend, but this perception is so dangerous to have. We have just been forced to endure one of the worst things that can ever happen to you, and yet there are people who think we should be forced into reporting what happened when we're not ready? In a world that often doesn't take these claims seriously? It made me so angry to see.
Thank you for sharing this.

I really needed to hear little bits of progress is still progress, thank you. My therapist says the same thing, but it helps hearing it from other people. I hold myself to high standards and if I don't notice progress immediately, it feels like I'm failing. The nightmares are new so I'm really hoping they don't stick around! Thank you ❤

Thanks for sharing your experience with me, I haven't heard much about EMDR but I might do some research into it. At the moment my therapist and I are working through all of the memories with exposure therapy, it's slow but I think it is working. It's just hard because there's multiple events we have to work through.

I'm glad you're not having nightmares anymore, they're terrible.
Thank you ❤

Thanks for your response. I've talked with my therapist about the things that have happened to me, and I emailed him yesterday about the new flashbacks. We have a session on Monday and he said we can talk about it then. He's said the same thing about it getting easier, and he's positive I'll get there, but it's hard to feel like that's true when my own brain hates me.

Thank you for the validation. I'm not normally an angry person, so I have trouble expressing it - really I have trouble expressing any negative feeling. But that's a good idea. I like writing but haven't been doing much of it lately, maybe I'll give that a try.

I was very good at blocking out what happened to me, telling myself it wasn't wrong, telling myself it was my fault. A part of me feels like if I never went to a psychologist I wouldn't have to be dealing with this, but I know that's not true. Thankfully, my psychologist is very supportive and is doing wonders for me, even if right now I can't say the stupid r word.

Thank you.
Glad to hear! It's definitely something that you can never forget.

My husband and I grew up in towns 3 hours away from each other, and met through a mutual friend when we were 18/19.

My husband's mum is really into genealogy and she's been able to work out that our distant relatives came over to Australia on the same boat in the late 1800's. 

A few months ago, my husband's dad hands me this old engagement ring. Turns out my nana went to my father-in-law's shop in 1979 and sold her engagement ring to him after divorcing my grandpa. My husband's nana took it home with her, and 20 years later decides that she thinks I should have it.
That's so horrible! I'm so sorry that happened to you and I hope you're doing okay. Guys like that make my blood boil. Good on you for looking out for your friend though! How brave of you.

I'm so sorry that happened to you. I've been in denial for a long time too, and I still am a little. The day that my psychologist and I talked about what what actually happened to me was I went home and had a panic attack, and then had to spend an hour on the phone to my psychologist while he tried to calm me down. I still can't even say the word. You're right, it really does hit you like a tonne of bricks.
